cues.zh: 我是个作家。
cues.en: I am a writer.

cues.zh: 写书是我的职业，但当然不止于此。
cues.en: Writing books is my profession but it's more than that, of course.

cues.zh: 它也是我一生挚爱与迷恋所在。
cues.en: It is also my great lifelong love and fascination.

cues.zh: 我不觉得这会有任何改变。
cues.en: And I don't expect that that's ever going to change.

cues.zh: 但话虽如此，最近发生了一件挺奇怪的事，
cues.en: But, that said, something kind of peculiar has happened recently

cues.zh: 在我的生活里，在我的事业中，
cues.en: in my life and in my career,

cues.zh: 它迫使我重新调整自己与这份工作的全部关系。
cues.en: which has caused me to have to recalibrate my whole relationship with this work.

cues.zh: 奇怪的是，我最近写了这本书，
cues.en: And the peculiar thing is that I recently wrote this book,

cues.zh: 这本叫《Eat, Pray, Love》的回忆录，
cues.en: this memoir called "Eat, Pray, Love"

cues.zh: 它显然不同于我以前的任何一本书，
cues.en: which, decidedly unlike any of my previous books,

cues.zh: 不知为何走向了世界，成了一件轰动性的、
cues.en: went out in the world for some reason, and became this big,

cues.zh: 超级现象级、国际畅销书的大事。
cues.en: mega-sensation, international bestseller thing.

cues.zh: 结果是，现在无论我走到哪儿，
cues.en: The result of which is that everywhere I go now,

cues.zh: 人们看我的眼神都像是我完蛋了。
cues.en: people treat me like I'm doomed.

cues.zh: 说真的——完蛋了，完蛋了！
cues.en: Seriously -- doomed, doomed!

cues.zh: 现在他们来找我，一脸担忧地说，
cues.en: Like, they come up to me now, all worried, and they say,

cues.zh: “你不怕再也写不出这么好的作品了吗？
cues.en: "Aren't you afraid you're never going to be able to top that?

cues.zh: 你不怕一辈子都在写作，
cues.en: Aren't you afraid you're going to keep writing for your whole life

cues.zh: 却再也写不出一本
cues.en: and you're never again going to create a book

cues.zh: 全世界没人在乎的书，
cues.en: that anybody in the world cares about at all,

cues.zh: 再也写不出来了吗？”
cues.en: ever again?"

cues.zh: 所以这还挺让人安心的。
cues.en: So that's reassuring, you know.

cues.zh: 但更糟的是，我恰好记得
cues.en: But it would be worse, except for that I happen to remember

cues.zh: 二十多年前，我还是个少年时，
cues.en: that over 20 years ago, when I was a teenager,

cues.zh: 当我第一次告诉别人我想当作家，
cues.en: when I first started telling people that I wanted to be a writer,

cues.zh: 我得到的也是这种基于恐惧的反应。
cues.en: I was met with this same sort of fear-based reaction.

cues.zh: 人们会说：“你不怕永远都不会成功吗？
cues.en: And people would say, "Aren't you afraid you're never going to have any success?

cues.zh: 你不怕被拒绝的羞辱会要了你的命吗？
cues.en: Aren't you afraid the humiliation of rejection will kill you?

cues.zh: 你不怕一辈子都在钻研这门手艺，
cues.en: Aren't you afraid that you're going to work your whole life at this craft

cues.zh: 却什么也做不出来，
cues.en: and nothing's ever going to come of it

cues.zh: 最后死在破碎梦想的废堆上，
cues.en: and you're going to die on a scrap heap of broken dreams

cues.zh: 满嘴都是失败的苦涩灰烬吗？”
cues.en: with your mouth filled with bitter ash of failure?"

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.zh: 就像那样，你知道的。
cues.en: Like that, you know.

cues.zh: 答案——对所有那些问题的简短回答是：“是的。”
cues.en: The answer -- the short answer to all those questions is, "Yes."

cues.zh: 是的，我害怕所有那些东西。
cues.en: Yes, I'm afraid of all those things.

cues.zh: 而且我一直都是这样。
cues.en: And I always have been.

cues.zh: 除了那些，我还害怕许许多多
cues.en: And I'm afraid of many, many more things besides

cues.zh: 别人甚至猜不到的东西，
cues.en: that people can't even guess at,

cues.zh: 比如海藻和其他吓人的东西。
cues.en: like seaweed and other things that are scary.

cues.zh: 但是，说到写作，
cues.en: But, when it comes to writing,

cues.zh: 我最近一直在思考、一直在琢磨的事情，
cues.en: the thing that I've been sort of thinking about lately, and wondering about lately,

cues.zh: 就是为什么？
cues.en: is why?

cues.zh: 你知道，这合理吗？
cues.en: You know, is it rational?

cues.zh: 合乎逻辑吗——竟然会有人被期望
cues.en: Is it logical that anybody should be expected

cues.zh: 害怕自己觉得天生就该做的工作。
cues.en: to be afraid of the work that they feel they were put on this Earth to do.

cues.zh: 而创意事业究竟特别在哪里，
cues.en: And what is it specifically about creative ventures

cues.zh: 似乎让我们特别担心彼此的心理健康，
cues.en: that seems to make us really nervous about each other's mental health

cues.zh: 而其他职业好像不会这样，你知道吗？
cues.en: in a way that other careers kind of don't do, you know?

cues.zh: 比如我爸爸，他就是个化学工程师
cues.en: Like my dad, for example, was a chemical engineer

cues.zh: 我不记得在他40年的化学工程生涯中
cues.en: and I don't recall once in his 40 years of chemical engineering

cues.zh: 有谁问过他是否害怕做个化学工程师，你知道吗？
cues.en: anybody asking him if he was afraid to be a chemical engineer, you know?

cues.zh: “那个化学工程区的，约翰，进展怎么样？”
cues.en: "That chemical-engineering block, John, how's it going?"

cues.zh: 这种事根本不会那样被提起，你知道吗？
cues.en: It just didn't come up like that, you know?

cues.zh: 但平心而论，化学工程师作为一个群体
cues.en: But to be fair, chemical engineers as a group

cues.zh: 几个世纪以来并没有真正赢得过
cues.en: haven't really earned a reputation over the centuries

cues.zh: 酗酒躁郁的名声。
cues.en: for being alcoholic manic-depressives.

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.zh: 我们作家，确实有点那样的名声，
cues.en: We writers, we kind of do have that reputation,

cues.zh: 不只是作家，而是各个领域的创意人士，
cues.en: and not just writers, but creative people across all genres,

cues.zh: 似乎都有这种精神极度不稳定的名声。
cues.en: it seems, have this reputation for being enormously mentally unstable.

cues.zh: 你只需看看那非常严峻的死亡人数
cues.en: And all you have to do is look at the very grim death count

cues.zh: 仅20世纪，那些真正杰出的创意头脑
cues.en: in the 20th century alone, of really magnificent creative minds

cues.zh: 英年早逝，而且往往是亲手结束生命，你知道吗？
cues.en: who died young and often at their own hands, you know?

cues.zh: 甚至那些没有真的自杀的人
cues.en: And even the ones who didn't literally commit suicide

cues.zh: 似乎也真的被自己的天赋毁了。
cues.en: seem to be really undone by their gifts, you know.

cues.zh: Norman Mailer 去世前的最后一次采访中说：
cues.en: Norman Mailer, just before he died, last interview, he said,

cues.zh: “我的每一本书都多杀死了一点我。”
cues.en: "Every one of my books has killed me a little more."

cues.zh: 用这样的话来谈论自己毕生的事业，真是非同寻常。
cues.en: An extraordinary statement to make about your life's work.

cues.zh: 但听到有人这么说时，我们连眼睛都不眨一下，
cues.en: But we don't even blink when we hear somebody say this,

cues.zh: 因为这类说法我们听得太久了，
cues.en: because we've heard that kind of stuff for so long

cues.zh: 而且不知怎的，我们已经完全内化并集体接受了
cues.en: and somehow we've completely internalized and accepted collectively

cues.zh: 这种观念：创造力和痛苦在本质上存在某种关联，
cues.en: this notion that creativity and suffering are somehow inherently linked

cues.zh: 而艺术才能最终总会导致痛苦。
cues.en: and that artistry, in the end, will always ultimately lead to anguish.

cues.zh: 今天我想问在座各位的问题是：
cues.en: And the question that I want to ask everybody here today

cues.zh: 你们都觉得这个想法没问题吗？
cues.en: is are you guys all cool with that idea?

cues.zh: 你们对此感到自在吗？
cues.en: Are you comfortable with that?

cues.zh: 因为哪怕从一英寸外看它，你知道——
cues.en: Because you look at it even from an inch away and, you know --

cues.zh: 我完全无法接受那种假设。
cues.en: I'm not at all comfortable with that assumption.

cues.zh: 我觉得它令人厌恶。
cues.en: I think it's odious.

cues.zh: 我也觉得它很危险，
cues.en: And I also think it's dangerous,

cues.zh: 我不想看到它延续到下个世纪。
cues.en: and I don't want to see it perpetuated into the next century.

cues.zh: 我认为更好的做法是鼓励我们伟大的创造性头脑活下去。
cues.en: I think it's better if we encourage our great creative minds to live.

cues.zh: 而且我明确知道，就我而言——在我的处境下——
cues.en: And I definitely know that, in my case -- in my situation --

cues.zh: 开始滑向那条黑暗之路对我来说会非常危险
cues.en: it would be very dangerous for me to start sort of leaking down that dark path

cues.zh: 关于假设，
cues.en: of assumption,

cues.zh: 尤其考虑到我目前所处的职业阶段。
cues.en: particularly given the circumstance that I'm in right now in my career.

cues.zh: 也就是——你知道，看看吧，
cues.en: Which is -- you know, like check it out,

cues.zh: 我还挺年轻的，我才40岁左右。
cues.en: I'm pretty young, I'm only about 40 years old.

cues.zh: 我大概还能再工作四十年。
cues.en: I still have maybe another four decades of work left in me.

cues.zh: 而且极有可能，我从现在起写的任何东西
cues.en: And it's exceedingly likely that anything I write from this point forward

cues.zh: 都会被世人评判为是在
cues.en: is going to be judged by the world as the work that came after

cues.zh: 我上一本书那种反常的成功之后的作品，对吧？
cues.en: the freakish success of my last book, right?

cues.zh: 我就直说吧，反正现在大家都是朋友了——
cues.en: I should just put it bluntly, because we're all sort of friends here now --

cues.zh: 我这辈子最大的成功，很可能已经过去了。
cues.en: it's exceedingly likely that my greatest success is behind me.

cues.zh: 天哪，这想法真够吓人的！
cues.en: So Jesus, what a thought!

cues.zh: 这种念头会让人
cues.en: That's the kind of thought that could lead a person

cues.zh: 早上九点就开始灌杜松子酒，
cues.en: to start drinking gin at nine o'clock in the morning,

cues.zh: 我可不想走到那一步。
cues.en: and I don't want to go there.

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.zh: 我更愿意继续做我热爱的这份工作。
cues.en: I would prefer to keep doing this work that I love.

cues.zh: 那么问题就来了：怎么做？
cues.en: And so, the question becomes, how?

cues.zh: 所以，经过反复思考，我觉得
cues.en: And so, it seems to me, upon a lot of reflection,

cues.zh: 为了继续写作，我现在必须采取的工作方式，
cues.en: that the way that I have to work now, in order to continue writing,

cues.zh: 就是给自己建立某种保护性的心理结构，对吧？
cues.en: is that I have to create some sort of protective psychological construct, right?

cues.zh: 我得想办法保持一段安全的距离，
cues.en: I have to sort of find some way to have a safe distance

cues.zh: 隔开正在写作的我，和我那种非常自然的焦虑——
cues.en: between me, as I am writing, and my very natural anxiety

cues.zh: 焦虑的是，从现在起，别人会怎么看待我的作品。
cues.en: about what the reaction to that writing is going to be, from now on.

cues.zh: 过去一年里，我一直在寻找
cues.en: And, as I've been looking, over the last year,

cues.zh: 能实现这一点的模型，
cues.en: for models for how to do that,

cues.zh: 我跨越时间维度去探寻，
cues.en: I've been sort of looking across time,

cues.zh: 试图找到其他的社会
cues.en: and I've been trying to find other societies

cues.zh: 看看他们是否有比我们更好、更明智的想法
cues.en: to see if they might have had better and saner ideas than we have

cues.zh: 关于如何帮助有创造力的人
cues.en: about how to help creative people

cues.zh: 去应对创造力本身所固有的情感风险。
cues.en: sort of manage the inherent emotional risks of creativity.

cues.zh: 这一探寻把我引向了古希腊和古罗马。
cues.en: And that search has led me to ancient Greece and ancient Rome.

cues.zh: 请耐心听我说，因为话题确实会绕回来。
cues.en: So stay with me, because it does circle around and back.

cues.zh: 但是，古希腊和古罗马——
cues.en: But, ancient Greece and ancient Rome --

cues.zh: 那时候人们并不认为创造力
cues.en: people did not happen to believe that creativity

cues.zh: 来自人类自身，明白吗？
cues.en: came from human beings back then, OK?

cues.zh: 人们相信创造力是一种神圣的守护神灵
cues.en: People believed that creativity was this divine attendant spirit

cues.zh: 它从某个遥远而不可知的源头降临到人身上，
cues.en: that came to human beings from some distant and unknowable source,

cues.zh: 出于遥远而不可知的原因。
cues.en: for distant and unknowable reasons.

cues.zh: 希腊人把这些富有创造力的神圣守护灵称为“daemons”。
cues.en: The Greeks famously called these divine attendant spirits of creativity "daemons."

cues.zh: 苏格拉底就 famously 相信自己有一个 daemon
cues.en: Socrates, famously, believed that he had a daemon

cues.zh: 从远方为他传递智慧。
cues.en: who spoke wisdom to him from afar.

cues.zh: 罗马人也有同样的想法，
cues.en: The Romans had the same idea,

cues.zh: 但他们把这种无形的创造之灵称为“genius”。
cues.en: but they called that sort of disembodied creative spirit a genius.

cues.zh: 这很棒，因为罗马人其实并不认为
cues.en: Which is great, because the Romans did not actually think

cues.zh: genius 是一个特别聪明的人。
cues.en: that a genius was a particularly clever individual.

cues.zh: 他们相信 genius 是一种神奇的神圣实体，
cues.en: They believed that a genius was this, sort of magical divine entity,

cues.zh: 据说它真的住在艺术家工作室的墙壁里，
cues.en: who was believed to literally live in the walls of an artist's studio,

cues.zh: 有点像家养小精灵多比，
cues.en: kind of like Dobby the house elf,

cues.zh: 它会出来
cues.en: and who would come out

cues.zh: 无形中协助艺术家的工作
cues.en: and sort of invisibly assist the artist with their work

cues.zh: 并塑造作品的结果。
cues.en: and would shape the outcome of that work.

cues.zh: 太妙了——就在那里，正是我说的那种距离——
cues.en: So brilliant -- there it is, right there, that distance that I'm talking about --

cues.zh: 那种保护你免受自己作品结果影响的心理建构。
cues.en: that psychological construct to protect you from the results of your work.

cues.zh: 大家都知道它就是那样运作的，对吧？
cues.en: And everyone knew that this is how it functioned, right?

cues.zh: 所以古代艺术家在某些方面是受到保护的，
cues.en: So the ancient artist was protected from certain things,

cues.zh: 比如说，免于过度自恋，对吧？
cues.en: like, for example, too much narcissism, right?

cues.zh: 如果你的作品很出色，你不能把功劳全揽在自己身上，
cues.en: If your work was brilliant, you couldn't take all the credit for it,

cues.zh: 大家都知道你有一位无形的天才在帮你。
cues.en: everybody knew that you had this disembodied genius who had helped you.

cues.zh: 如果你的作品砸了，也不全是你的错，懂吧？
cues.en: If your work bombed, not entirely your fault, you know?

cues.zh: 大家都知道你那位天才有点不靠谱。
cues.en: Everyone knew your genius was kind of lame.

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.zh: 西方人就是这样看待创造力的，
cues.en: And this is how people thought about creativity in the West

cues.zh: 持续了很长很长时间。
cues.en: for a really long time.

cues.zh: 然后文艺复兴来了，一切都变了，
cues.en: And then the Renaissance came and everything changed,

cues.zh: 我们有了一个伟大的想法，这个伟大的想法就是，
cues.en: and we had this big idea, and the big idea was,

cues.zh: 把个体的人放在宇宙的中心，
cues.en: let's put the individual human being at the center of the universe

cues.zh: 凌驾于所有神明与奥秘之上，
cues.en: above all gods and mysteries,

cues.zh: 再也没有空间留给那些
cues.en: and there's no more room for mystical creatures

cues.zh: 听命于神灵的神秘造物了。
cues.en: who take dictation from the divine.

cues.zh: 这是理性人文主义的开端，
cues.en: And it's the beginning of rational humanism,

cues.zh: 人们开始相信，创造力
cues.en: and people started to believe that creativity

cues.zh: 完全源自个体的自我。
cues.en: came completely from the self of the individual.

cues.zh: 历史上第一次，
cues.en: And for the first time in history,

cues.zh: 你开始听到人们说某某艺术家是个天才，
cues.en: you start to hear people referring to this or that artist as being a genius,

cues.zh: 而不是拥有天才。
cues.en: rather than having a genius.

cues.zh: 我得说，我认为那是个巨大的错误。
cues.en: And I got to tell you, I think that was a huge error.

cues.zh: 你知道，我认为让某个人，仅仅一个人
cues.en: You know, I think that allowing somebody, one mere person

cues.zh: 相信自己就是那个容器，
cues.en: to believe that he or she is like, the vessel,

cues.zh: 你知道，就像是所有神圣、创造性、不可知、永恒奥秘的
cues.en: you know, like the font and the essence and the source

cues.zh: 源泉和本质所在，
cues.en: of all divine, creative, unknowable, eternal mystery

cues.zh: 把这种责任压在一个脆弱的人类心灵上，实在是有点太重了。
cues.en: is just a smidge too much responsibility to put on one fragile, human psyche.

cues.zh: 这就像让人吞下太阳。
cues.en: It's like asking somebody to swallow the sun.

cues.zh: 它完全扭曲和歪曲了自我，
cues.en: It just completely warps and distorts egos,

cues.zh: 并制造出所有这些关于表现的难以驾驭的期望。
cues.en: and it creates all these unmanageable expectations about performance.

cues.zh: 我觉得那种压力
cues.en: And I think the pressure of that

cues.zh: 在过去500年里一直扼杀着我们的艺术家。
cues.en: has been killing off our artists for the last 500 years.

cues.zh: 如果这是真的，
cues.en: And, if this is true,

cues.zh: 而且我认为确实如此，
cues.en: and I think it is true,

cues.zh: 问题就变成了：现在怎么办？
cues.en: the question becomes, what now?

cues.zh: 我们能换种方式做吗？
cues.en: Can we do this differently?

cues.zh: 也许回到更古老的认知
cues.en: Maybe go back to some more ancient understanding

cues.zh: 关于人类与创意奥秘之间的关系。
cues.en: about the relationship between humans and the creative mystery.

cues.zh: 也许不行。
cues.en: Maybe not.

cues.zh: 也许我们无法仅凭一场18分钟的演讲
cues.en: Maybe we can't just erase 500 years of rational humanistic thought

cues.zh: 就抹去500年的理性人文思想。
cues.en: in one 18 minute speech.

cues.zh: 而且在座可能有人
cues.en: And there's probably people in this audience

cues.zh: 会提出非常合理的科学质疑
cues.en: who would raise really legitimate scientific suspicions

cues.zh: 关于基本上就是仙女
cues.en: about the notion of, basically, fairies

cues.zh: 跟着人们，往他们的项目上抹仙女汁之类的说法。
cues.en: who follow people around rubbing fairy juice on their projects and stuff.

cues.zh: 我大概没法让大家都认同我这一点。
cues.en: I'm not, probably, going to bring you all along with me on this.

cues.zh: 但我想提出的问题是——
cues.en: But the question that I kind of want to pose is --

cues.zh: 你知道，为什么不呢？
cues.en: you know, why not?

cues.zh: 为什么不换个角度想想呢？
cues.en: Why not think about it this way?

cues.zh: 因为在我听过的所有解释里，这个说法同样说得通
cues.en: Because it makes as much sense as anything else I have ever heard

cues.zh: 用来解释那种令人抓狂的反复无常
cues.en: in terms of explaining the utter maddening capriciousness

cues.zh: 也就是创作过程。
cues.en: of the creative process.

cues.zh: 这个过程，任何尝试过创作的人——
cues.en: A process which, as anybody who has ever tried to make something --

cues.zh: 基本上在座各位都算——
cues.en: which is to say basically everyone here ---

cues.zh: 都知道它并不总是遵循理性。
cues.en: knows does not always behave rationally.

cues.zh: 事实上，有时感觉简直像是灵异现象。
cues.en: And, in fact, can sometimes feel downright paranormal.

cues.zh: 我最近有这么一次经历
cues.en: I had this encounter recently

cues.zh: 遇见了一位了不起的美国诗人Ruth Stone，
cues.en: where I met the extraordinary American poet Ruth Stone,

cues.zh: 她现在已经九十多岁了，但一辈子都在写诗
cues.en: who's now in her 90s, but she's been a poet her entire life

cues.zh: 她告诉我，她小时候在弗吉尼亚乡下长大，
cues.en: and she told me that when she was growing up in rural Virginia,

cues.zh: 经常在田里干活，
cues.en: she would be out working in the fields,

cues.zh: 她说她能感觉到、也能听到一首诗
cues.en: and she said she would feel and hear a poem

cues.zh: 从远处的风景中向她飞来。
cues.en: coming at her from over the landscape.

cues.zh: 她说那就像一阵雷鸣般的空气。
cues.en: And she said it was like a thunderous train of air.

cues.zh: 它会越过风景，朝她疾驰而来。
cues.en: And it would come barreling down at her over the landscape.

cues.zh: 她能感觉到它逼近，因为它会震动她脚下的土地。
cues.en: And she felt it coming, because it would shake the earth under her feet.

cues.zh: 她知道那一刻她只有一件事要做，
cues.en: She knew that she had only one thing to do at that point,

cues.zh: 用她的话说，就是“拼命跑”。
cues.en: and that was to, in her words, "run like hell."

cues.zh: 她会拼命跑向屋子
cues.en: And she would run like hell to the house

cues.zh: 而这首诗会在后面追她，
cues.en: and she would be getting chased by this poem,

cues.zh: 关键在于她必须拿到纸和笔，
cues.en: and the whole deal was that she had to get to a piece of paper and a pencil

cues.zh: 快到当它轰然穿过她时，她能把它收住
cues.en: fast enough so that when it thundered through her, she could collect it

cues.zh: 把它抓在纸上。
cues.en: and grab it on the page.

cues.zh: 有时候她不够快，
cues.en: And other times she wouldn't be fast enough,

cues.zh: 于是一直跑一直跑，却到不了屋子
cues.en: so she'd be running and running, and she wouldn't get to the house

cues.zh: 诗就会轰然穿过她，她就错过了
cues.en: and the poem would barrel through her and she would miss it

cues.zh: 她说它会继续越过风景，
cues.en: and she said it would continue on across the landscape,

cues.zh: 用她的话说，“去寻找另一位诗人”。
cues.en: looking, as she put it "for another poet."

cues.zh: 然后有这样一些时刻——
cues.en: And then there were these times --

cues.zh: 这是我一直忘不掉的一段——
cues.en: this is the piece I never forgot --

cues.zh: 她说有些瞬间她几乎会怀念那种感觉，对吧？
cues.en: she said that there were moments where she would almost miss it, right?

cues.zh: 于是，她跑向房子，寻找那张纸
cues.en: So, she's running to the house and she's looking for the paper

cues.zh: 那首诗从她身上穿过，
cues.en: and the poem passes through her,

cues.zh: 就在它穿过她的瞬间，她抓起一支铅笔，
cues.en: and she grabs a pencil just as it's going through her,

cues.zh: 然后她说，就像她会伸出另一只手
cues.en: and then she said, it was like she would reach out with her other hand

cues.zh: 把它抓住。
cues.en: and she would catch it.

cues.zh: 她会抓住那首诗的尾巴，
cues.en: She would catch the poem by its tail,

cues.zh: 把它往回拉进自己的身体
cues.en: and she would pull it backwards into her body

cues.zh: 一边在纸上誊写。
cues.en: as she was transcribing on the page.

cues.zh: 而在这些时刻，诗会完美而完整地出现在纸上
cues.en: And in these instances, the poem would come up on the page perfect and intact

cues.zh: 但是倒着的，从最后一个词到第一个词。
cues.en: but backwards, from the last word to the first.

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.zh: 所以当我听到这个时，我心想——这太不可思议了，
cues.en: So when I heard that I was like -- that's uncanny,

cues.zh: 这跟我的创作过程简直一模一样。
cues.en: that's exactly what my creative process is like.

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.zh: 我的创作过程根本不是这样的——我不是流水线！
cues.en: That's not at all what my creative process is -- I'm not the pipeline!

cues.zh: 我是一头骡子，我工作方式就是
cues.en: I'm a mule, and the way that I have to work

cues.zh: 每天必须同一时间起床，
cues.en: is I have to get up at the same time every day,

cues.zh: 流汗、苦干，笨拙地硬扛过去。
cues.en: and sweat and labor and barrel through it really awkwardly.

cues.zh: 但即便是我，带着这股骡子脾气，
cues.en: But even I, in my mulishness,

cues.zh: 即便是我，有时候也触碰到那个东西。
cues.en: even I have brushed up against that thing, at times.

cues.zh: 我猜你们很多人也是。
cues.en: And I would imagine that a lot of you have too.

cues.zh: 你知道，即便是我，也有作品或想法通过我而来，来自某个
cues.en: You know, even I have had work or ideas come through me from a source

cues.zh: 我实在无法识别的源头。
cues.en: that I honestly cannot identify.

cues.zh: 那到底是什么东西？
cues.en: And what is that thing?

cues.zh: 我们该如何与之相处，才不会让我们失去理智，
cues.en: And how are we to relate to it in a way that will not make us lose our minds,

cues.zh: 反而可能让我们保持清醒？
cues.en: but, in fact, might actually keep us sane?

cues.zh: 对我来说，关于如何做到这一点，最好的当代例子
cues.en: And for me, the best contemporary example that I have of how to do that

cues.zh: 是音乐人Tom Waits，
cues.en: is the musician Tom Waits,

cues.zh: 几年前我因一篇杂志约稿采访过他。
cues.en: who I got to interview several years ago on a magazine assignment.

cues.zh: 我们之前聊过这个，
cues.en: And we were talking about this,

cues.zh: 你知道，Tom一生中大部分时间，几乎就是
cues.en: and you know, Tom, for most of his life, he was pretty much the embodiment

cues.zh: 那种饱受折磨的当代现代艺术家的化身，
cues.en: of the tormented contemporary modern artist,

cues.zh: 试图控制、管理和支配
cues.en: trying to control and manage and dominate

cues.zh: 那些难以驾驭的创作冲动，
cues.en: these sort of uncontrollable creative impulses

cues.zh: 而它们完全是内化的。
cues.en: that were totally internalized.

cues.zh: 但后来他年纪大了，变得平和了，
cues.en: But then he got older, he got calmer,

cues.zh: 有一天他在洛杉矶开车行驶在高速公路上，
cues.en: and one day he was driving down the freeway in Los Angeles,

cues.zh: 就在那时，一切为他改变了。
cues.en: and this is when it all changed for him.

cues.zh: 他一路飞驰，突然间
cues.en: And he's speeding along, and all of a sudden

cues.zh: 他听到一小段旋律，
cues.en: he hears this little fragment of melody,

cues.zh: 那旋律进入他的脑海，就像灵感常常降临那样，难以捉摸又令人心动，
cues.en: that comes into his head as inspiration often comes, elusive and tantalizing,

cues.zh: 他想要它，它太美妙了，
cues.en: and he wants it, it's gorgeous,

cues.zh: 他渴望得到它，却毫无办法。
cues.en: and he longs for it, but he has no way to get it.

cues.zh: 他没有纸，没有铅笔，也没有录音机。
cues.en: He doesn't have a piece of paper, or a pencil, or a tape recorder.

cues.zh: 于是他开始感到那种旧日的焦虑又在心中升起
cues.en: So he starts to feel all of that old anxiety start to rise in him

cues.zh: 就像，“我要失去这个东西了，
cues.en: like, "I'm going to lose this thing,

cues.zh: 我会被这首歌永远纠缠。
cues.en: and I'll be be haunted by this song forever.

cues.zh: 我不够好，我做不到。”
cues.en: I'm not good enough, and I can't do it."

cues.zh: 他没有惊慌，而是停了下来。
cues.en: And instead of panicking, he just stopped.

cues.zh: 他停住了整个心理过程，做了一件全新的事。
cues.en: He just stopped that whole mental process and he did something completely novel.

cues.zh: 他抬头看天，说道，
cues.en: He just looked up at the sky, and he said,

cues.zh: “打扰一下，你看不出我正在开车吗？”
cues.en: "Excuse me, can you not see that I'm driving?"

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.zh: “我看起来像是现在能写下一首歌吗？
cues.en: "Do I look like I can write down a song right now?

cues.zh: 如果你真的想存在，找个更合适的时机再来
cues.en: If you really want to exist, come back at a more opportune moment

cues.zh: 等我能照顾你的时候。
cues.en: when I can take care of you.

cues.zh: 不然的话，今天去找别人吧。
cues.en: Otherwise, go bother somebody else today.

cues.zh: 去找Leonard Cohen吧。”
cues.en: Go bother Leonard Cohen."

cues.zh: 之后他的整个工作流程都变了。
cues.en: And his whole work process changed after that.

cues.zh: 不是工作本身，工作往往还是像以前一样黑暗。
cues.en: Not the work, the work was still oftentimes as dark as ever.

cues.zh: 但这个过程，以及围绕它的沉重焦虑
cues.en: But the process, and the heavy anxiety around it

cues.zh: 在他把那个精灵、那个天才从体内释放出来时消散了
cues.en: was released when he took the genie, the genius out of him

cues.zh: 那个东西在那里只会制造麻烦，他把它放回了它来的地方，
cues.en: where it was causing nothing but trouble, and released it back where it came from,

cues.zh: 并意识到这不必是这种内化的、折磨人的东西。
cues.en: and realized that this didn't have to be this internalized, tormented thing.

cues.zh: 它可以是这种奇特的、奇妙的、怪异的协作，
cues.en: It could be this peculiar, wondrous, bizarre collaboration,

cues.zh: 像是 Tom 和那个陌生的、外在的东西之间的对话
cues.en: kind of conversation between Tom and the strange, external thing

cues.zh: 那个并不完全是 Tom 的东西。
cues.en: that was not quite Tom.

cues.zh: 当我听到那个故事时，它开始稍微改变
cues.en: When I heard that story, it started to shift a little bit

cues.zh: 我工作的方式，而这个想法已经救过我一次。
cues.en: the way that I worked too, and this idea already saved me once.

cues.zh: 它在我写《美食、祈祷、恋爱》写到一半时救了我，
cues.en: It saved me when I was in the middle of writing "Eat, Pray, Love,"

cues.zh: 我陷入了那种绝望的深渊
cues.en: and I fell into one of those sort of pits of despair

cues.zh: 我们所有人都会在写东西却写不出来时陷入的那种
cues.en: that we all fall into when we're working on something and it's not coming

cues.zh: 然后你开始想这会是一场灾难，是有史以来最糟糕的书。
cues.en: and you start to think this is going to be a disaster, the worst book ever written.

cues.zh: 不只是糟糕，而是史上最烂的书。
cues.en: Not just bad, but the worst book ever written.

cues.zh: 我开始想，干脆放弃这个项目算了。
cues.en: And I started to think I should just dump this project.

cues.zh: 但后来我记起Tom对着空气说话的样子
cues.en: But then I remembered Tom talking to the open air

cues.zh: 于是我试了试。
cues.en: and I tried it.

cues.zh: 我 just 从手稿上抬起头
cues.en: So I just lifted my face up from the manuscript

cues.zh: 把话对着房间一个空荡荡的角落说。
cues.en: and I directed my comments to an empty corner of the room.

cues.zh: 我大声说：“听着，你这家伙，
cues.en: And I said aloud, "Listen you, thing,

cues.zh: 你我都清楚，如果这本书不精彩
cues.en: you and I both know that if this book isn't brilliant

cues.zh: 那并不全是我的错，对吧？
cues.en: that is not entirely my fault, right?

cues.zh: 因为你看得出，我已经倾尽全力了，
cues.en: Because you can see that I am putting everything I have into this,

cues.zh: 我没有更多可以拿出来的了。
cues.en: I don't have any more than this.

cues.zh: 你要是想让它更好，你就得现身，履行你那部分约定。
cues.en: If you want it to be better, you've got to show up and do your part of the deal.

cues.zh: 但如果你不这么做，那你知道么，去他的。
cues.en: But if you don't do that, you know what, the hell with it.

cues.zh: 我反正会继续写下去，因为那是我的工作。
cues.en: I'm going to keep writing anyway because that's my job.

cues.zh: 我希望今天能被记录下来，
cues.en: And I would please like the record to reflect today

cues.zh: 证明我履行了我这部分的职责。”
cues.en: that I showed up for my part of the job."

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.zh: 因为——
cues.en: Because --

cues.zh: （掌声）
cues.en: (Applause)

cues.zh: 因为说到底就是这样，好吧——
cues.en: Because in the end it's like this, OK --

cues.zh: 几个世纪前，在北非的沙漠里，
cues.en: centuries ago in the deserts of North Africa,

cues.zh: 人们常常聚在一起，参加这些月光下的神圣舞蹈与音乐之夜，
cues.en: people used to gather for these moonlight dances of sacred dance and music

cues.zh: 一连持续好几个小时，直到黎明。
cues.en: that would go on for hours and hours, until dawn.

cues.zh: 这些表演总是很壮观，因为舞者都是专业水准，
cues.en: They were always magnificent, because the dancers were professionals

cues.zh: 他们非常出色，对吧？
cues.en: and they were terrific, right?

cues.zh: 但偶尔，极其罕见地，会发生一些事，
cues.en: But every once in a while, very rarely, something would happen,

cues.zh: 其中一位表演者会真正进入超凡的境界。
cues.en: and one of these performers would actually become transcendent.

cues.zh: 我知道你们明白我在说什么，
cues.en: And I know you know what I'm talking about,

cues.zh: 因为我知道你们一生中某个时刻都见过
cues.en: because I know you've all seen, at some point in your life,

cues.zh: 这样的表演。
cues.en: a performance like this.

cues.zh: 就好像时间停止了，
cues.en: It was like time would stop,

cues.zh: 舞者仿佛穿过了某种门户，
cues.en: and the dancer would sort of step through some kind of portal

cues.zh: 他做的动作并没有什么不同，
cues.en: and he wasn't doing anything different

cues.zh: 和他之前一千个夜晚做过的一模一样，
cues.en: than he had ever done, 1,000 nights before,

cues.zh: 但一切都恰到好处地契合了。
cues.en: but everything would align.

cues.zh: 突然间，他看起来不再只是凡人。
cues.en: And all of a sudden, he would no longer appear to be merely human.

cues.zh: 他会从内而外发光，从下方被照亮
cues.en: He would be lit from within, and lit from below

cues.zh: 全身燃起神圣的火焰。
cues.en: and all lit up on fire with divinity.

cues.zh: 当这发生时，那时候，
cues.en: And when this happened, back then,

cues.zh: 人们知道那是什么，你知道，他们直呼其名。
cues.en: people knew it for what it was, you know, they called it by its name.

cues.zh: 他们会双手合十，开始吟诵，
cues.en: They would put their hands together and they would start to chant,

cues.zh: “安拉，安拉，安拉，神，神，神。”
cues.en: "Allah, Allah, Allah, God, God, God."

cues.zh: 那就是神，你知道。
cues.en: That's God, you know.

cues.zh: 有趣的历史注脚：
cues.en: Curious historical footnote:

cues.zh: 当摩尔人入侵西班牙南部时，他们带去了这个习俗
cues.en: when the Moors invaded southern Spain, they took this custom with them

cues.zh: 几个世纪以来，发音发生了变化
cues.en: and the pronunciation changed over the centuries

cues.zh: 从“安拉，安拉，安拉”变成了“奥莱，奥莱，奥莱”
cues.en: from "Allah, Allah, Allah," to "Olé, olé, olé,"

cues.zh: 你在斗牛和弗拉门戈舞中仍能听到。
cues.en: which you still hear in bullfights and in flamenco dances.

cues.zh: 在西班牙，当表演者完成了某种不可思议的神奇之事，
cues.en: In Spain, when a performer has done something impossible and magic,

cues.zh: “安拉，奥莱，奥莱，安拉，精彩，太棒了”
cues.en: "Allah, olé, olé, Allah, magnificent, bravo,"

cues.zh: 难以言喻，就是这样——一瞥神迹。
cues.en: incomprehensible, there it is -- a glimpse of God.

cues.zh: 这很好，因为我们需要它。
cues.en: Which is great, because we need that.

cues.zh: 但麻烦的是第二天早上，
cues.en: But, the tricky bit comes the next morning,

cues.zh: 对舞者本人来说，当他醒来发现
cues.en: for the dancer himself, when he wakes up and discovers

cues.zh: 已经是周二上午11点，他不再是神的一瞥。
cues.en: that it's Tuesday at 11 a.m., and he's no longer a glimpse of God.

cues.zh: 他只是一个膝盖很糟的衰老凡人，
cues.en: He's just an aging mortal with really bad knees,

cues.zh: 也许他再也无法达到那样的高度。
cues.en: and maybe he's never going to ascend to that height again.

cues.zh: 也许再也没人会在旋转时高唱神的名字，
cues.en: And maybe nobody will ever chant God's name again as he spins,

cues.zh: 那他余生该怎么办？
cues.en: and what is he then to do with the rest of his life?

cues.zh: 这很难。
cues.en: This is hard.

cues.zh: 这是创作生涯中最痛苦的和解之一
cues.en: This is one of the most painful reconciliations to make

cues.zh: 在创作生活中。
cues.en: in a creative life.

cues.zh: 但也许不必如此充满痛苦
cues.en: But maybe it doesn't have to be quite so full of anguish

cues.zh: 如果你从一开始就没有碰巧相信，
cues.en: if you never happened to believe, in the first place,

cues.zh: 你身上最非凡的部分来自你自己。
cues.en: that the most extraordinary aspects of your being came from you.

cues.zh: 但也许如果你只是相信它们是借给你的
cues.en: But maybe if you just believed that they were on loan to you

cues.zh: 来自某个难以想象的源头，在你生命中一段美好的时光里
cues.en: from some unimaginable source for some exquisite portion of your life

cues.zh: 等你完成后传递下去，
cues.en: to be passed along when you're finished,

cues.zh: 交给别人。
cues.en: with somebody else.

cues.zh: 如果我们这样去想，一切就开始改变了。
cues.en: And, you know, if we think about it this way, it starts to change everything.

cues.zh: 我就是这么开始思考的，
cues.en: This is how I've started to think,

cues.zh: 过去几个月我一直是这么想的，
cues.en: and this is certainly how I've been thinking in the last few months

cues.zh: 因为我正在写一本即将出版的书，
cues.en: as I've been working on the book that will soon be published,

cues.zh: 它被危险地、可怕地过度期待，
cues.en: as the dangerously, frighteningly over-anticipated follow up

cues.zh: 作为我那反常成功的后续之作。
cues.en: to my freakish success.

cues.zh: 当我为此特别紧张的时候，
cues.en: And what I have to sort of keep telling myself

cues.zh: 我得不断告诉自己：别害怕。
cues.en: when I get really psyched out about that is don't be afraid.

cues.zh: 别被吓倒。做好你的事就行。
cues.en: Don't be daunted. Just do your job.

cues.zh: 继续守好你那一份，不管那是什么。
cues.en: Continue to show up for your piece of it, whatever that might be.

cues.zh: 如果你的工作是跳舞，那就跳你的舞。
cues.en: If your job is to dance, do your dance.

cues.zh: 如果分派给你的那位古怪的神圣天才，
cues.en: If the divine, cockeyed genius assigned to your case

cues.zh: 决定让某种奇妙的东西被瞥见，哪怕只有一瞬间，
cues.en: decides to let some sort of wonderment be glimpsed, for just one moment

cues.zh: 通过你的努力，那就“好耶！”
cues.en: through your efforts, then "Olé!"

cues.zh: 就算不会，也尽管跳你的舞。
cues.en: And if not, do your dance anyhow.

cues.zh: 但还是要对你说一声“Olé！”
cues.en: And "Olé!" to you, nonetheless.

cues.zh: 我相信这一点，也觉得我们必须把它教给别人。
cues.en: I believe this and I feel that we must teach it.

cues.zh: 还是要对你说一声“Olé！”，
cues.en: "Olé!" to you, nonetheless,

cues.zh: 只为那份纯粹的人类热爱与倔强，
cues.en: just for having the sheer human love and stubbornness

cues.zh: 让你一次次坚持出现。
cues.en: to keep showing up.

cues.zh: 谢谢。
cues.en: Thank you.

cues.zh: （掌声）
cues.en: (Applause)

cues.zh: 谢谢。
cues.en: Thank you.

cues.zh: （掌声）
cues.en: (Applause)

cues.zh: June Cohen：Olé！
cues.en: June Cohen: Olé!

cues.zh: （掌声）
cues.en: (Applause)
